items.title: Pricing Intelligence: Task-Based Learning and Labor Displacement in the AI Economy
items.desc: A microeconomic model in which AI providers sell access to users who complete tasks with AI or labor, and AI learns from the complex tasks delegated to it; the author shows a tension between profit maximization and complex-task learning that shapes the speed and direction of AI progress and labor displacement. [arXiv econ.TH, submitted 2026-08-11]

items.title: Beyond the Grid: Cost, Carbon, and Capital Requirements of On-Site Power Technologies for AI Data Centers
items.desc: Argues interconnection queues, not electricity prices, now determine where data centers can be built, and evaluates nine on-site power supply technologies for AI data centers on cost, carbon, and capital requirements. [arXiv econ.EM, announced 2026-08-11]

items.title: Dynamic Coalition Formation and Communication Pricing in Skill-Based Agentic AI Systems
items.desc: Models agent selection and communication as an economic problem in multi-agent LLM systems, where token cost, latency, and error propagation grow with active agents and links, and derives efficient coalition formation and communication-pricing rules. [arXiv econ.TH/cs.AI, announced 2026-08-11]

items.title: Innovating with Generative AI: A Human Bottleneck Framework
items.desc: Proposes a framework in which the key constraints on innovation are cognitive and social bottlenecks — how people generate ideas, evaluate novelty, and communicate — and analyzes how generative AI relaxes or shifts each bottleneck. [arXiv econ.GN/cs.HC, announced 2026-08-11]

items.title: AI Financial Advice: Supply, Demand, and Life Cycle Implications
items.desc: Has a representative sample write real prompts asking LLMs for spending and investing advice, then simulates lifetime outcomes of following it: GPT-5.2's advice moves households toward life-cycle theory (diversified equity participation, age-declining equity shares, bigger savings buffers), with recommendations varying by gender, AI experience, and financial literacy. [NBER w35574, issued August 2026, posted week of 2026-08-10]

items.title: Beyond Cash Flows: A Multi-Agent AI Framework for Valuing Clinical-Stage, Cross-Border Biotechnology
items.desc: Builds a collaborative multi-agent LLM system (analysts, researchers, risk managers) for valuing clinical-stage, cross-border biotech companies, addressing gaps in current AI-driven investment analysis beyond standard cash-flow methods. [arXiv q-fin.PM, submitted 2026-08-10, announced 2026-08-12]

items.title: Yield Curve Prediction with Machine Learning: Forecasting Approaches and the Role of Macroeconomic Predictors
items.desc: Compares direct-yield and factor-based machine learning approaches to U.S. Treasury yield-curve forecasting with a high-dimensional macro information set over a 2015-2025 out-of-sample period, finding gains over the random walk are concentrated in specific maturities and periods. [arXiv econ.GN/q-fin, announced 2026-08-11]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: When LLM Agents Negotiate: Private Information and Dynamic Bargaining in Supply Chains
items.desc: Benchmarks nine LLMs from OpenAI, Google, and Alibaba as autonomous procurement negotiators in a canonical supply chain bargaining problem — a buyer with private demand information negotiating a quantity-payment contract with an uninformed seller — asking whether delegated AI negotiators create value and avoid money-losing contracts. [arXiv cs.AI/econ.GN, announced 2026-08-11]

items.title: Nvidia's great silicon showdown
items.desc: Nvidia's biggest customers — Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft — are developing custom chips to reduce their dependence on the AI chipmaker, which is fighting back with a $500bn deal. [Economist, 2026-08-11]

items.title: The Perils of Wall St.'s Race to Pour Billions More Into A.I.
items.desc: Investors including BlackRock have committed enormous sums to lend to the AI industry, but not everyone shares the enthusiasm — DealBook examines the risks in the AI lending boom. [NYT DealBook, 2026-08-11]

items.title: An A.I.-Focused Buyer of Service Firms Raises $2 Billion
items.desc: Thrive Holdings, which acquires service businesses to infuse them with AI, raised $2 billion from backers including SoftBank — a bet on AI-driven roll-ups of traditional firms. [NYT DealBook, 2026-08-12]

items.title: Why the U.S. Economy Needs A.I. — Bubble or Not
items.desc: Opinion piece arguing the U.S. economy has become dependent on AI investment, using a hedge fund's $35 billion loss to probe the state of the industry and what a crash could mean. [NYT Opinion, 2026-08-12]
